title: Writing at the zipper frontier
statement: For an alphabet $A$, an integer frontier $z$, finite lists $l,r$ of possibly blank symbols, and a possibly blank symbol $b$, overwriting the represented tape at coordinate $z$ with $b$ gives the tape represented by the same frontier and left stack, with right stack obtained by prepending $b$ to the tail of $r$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite lists $l,r$ of possibly blank symbols
replaced:
Consider the two-way infinite partial tape assembled from a position $z \in \mathbb{Z}$,
a list $r$ of optional symbols occupying cells $z, z+1, \dots$, and a list $l$ occupying
cells $z-1, z-2, \dots$ (all unlisted cells blank). Overwriting the cell at $z$ with a
value $b$ yields the tape assembled from $z$, $l$, and the list whose first entry is $b$
followed by the tail of $r$.
